title: How Does the Adoption of Ad Blockers Affect News Consumption?
eligible_reason: Design is staggered (user-specific adoption weeks 12-16, never-adopters as controls) with user and week FE, but every main-text specification is estimated on a coarsened-exact-matching (CEM) matched sample, which PROTOCOL.md Section 2 excludes as matching-based DiD. The unmatched version appears only in a Web Appendix. Data are proprietary and no package is available, so replication is infeasible regardless.
design_notes: Equation 1: Y_it = a_i + d_t + b1 I1_it + b2 I2_it + e_it, with Y = log(1 + article views) or log(1 + breadth). Primary analysis: adopters (6,366 users adopting in weeks 12-16; cohorts 1,124 / 3,269 / 1,167 / 384 / 422) vs. nonadopters (38,270 users), then CEM on demographics, pre-treatment behavior, first/last observed week, browser; matched sample 574 treated and 748 control users, 9,370 user-weeks. Estimation window weeks 7-16. Table 4 cols 1-2 (Ad Blocker Adoption): article views b1 .297 (.038), b2 .155 (.049); breadth b1 .198 (.027), b2 .096 (.036); N = 9,370. Cols 3-4 (early adopters wk 12 vs late adopters wk 14, N = 1,423) have a single treatment date. Cols 5-6 (abandonment, N = 1,009) also matched. Tables 5 and 6 re-estimate the same matched specification for mechanism outcomes and subsamples. The abstract's 21.0%-43.2% increase in articles read comes from Table 4 col 1. SEs clustered by user.
estimators_reported: TWFE with user and week FE on CEM-matched sample (Tables 4-6)
propensity-score-matching and unmatched robustness (Web Appendix only)

screener_notes: Marked ineligible only because of the matching exclusion; treat as the one borderline paper in this batch. If the lead relaxes the matching rule, candidate specs are Table 4 cols 1-2 (primary, in abstract), Table 5 Panels A-B (10 outcomes, same specification), Table 6 (subsamples), plus the abandonment columns (Table 4 cols 5-6) which may also be staggered. Unmatched estimates exist only in the Web Appendix (Tables W20 etc.), not in the main text. Data: proprietary clickstream from an anonymous European news publisher; not obtainable without the publisher. No replication package was listed in the batch file (package_dir and regressions_path empty); screening is from the article text only.
